newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Five killed as Greek carrier sinks off S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Five killed as Greek carrier sinks off S.Africa.

text.p: At least five seamen died when a Greek-registered iron ore carrier sank off South Africa's Indian Ocean coast on Saturday, the port authority said.

The 74,278 tonne Iollos Victor sank at about 0630 GMT on Saturday, 107 nautical miles south of Cape St Francis near the Indian Ocean city of Port Elizabeth, assistant port captain Brian Phipps told Reuters.

Phipps said four bodies were found in the sea and the fifth victim was one of the 21 sailors earlier rescued by a Japanese fishing trawler, the Ryoun Maru 18, which had also responded to the crew's distress call at 0540 GMT on Saturday.
"We picked up four bodies from the sea (but) we have now discovered that there are 15 people and one dead body on the trawler which is still fighting its way to Port Elizabeth," he said.
"Due to continuing bad weather conditions in the area, the trawler is now expected to dock with the 15 survivors at about 1 a.m. (2300 GMT) tomorrow (Sunday)," Phipps added.
The rest of the crew, which had totalled 25, had been rescued by a helicopter shuttle service launched early on Saturday to transport the survivors, some suffering from hypothermia, to hospital.
The ill-fated carrier had been taking in water in its forward hatches before it sank and Phipps said bad weather condition had exacerbated the problem.
"There are big swells of about six metres and it is raining hard there," he added.
A Port Elizabeth ambulanceman helping with the rescue, Lungile Yekela, told Reuters the Iollos Victor had been en route from the Philippines to Port Elizabeth when it sank.
